value.rationale: Mann–Whitney and Cramér–von Mises are canonical two-sample rank procedures targeting different aspects of departure from a common distribution. The formula quantifies their null coupling at finite sample size and reveals a nonvanishing universal proportional-sample limit of 1/5 after squaring and standardizing the location component. This is useful for joint calibration, combined testing, and understanding the component structure of omnibus rank statistics, rather than being an arbitrary parameter slice.
